{"answer":"#!/bin/sh
# count_lines_with_word.sh
# Usage:
# 1) Called by init script that sets WORD and FILES (space-separated):
#    WORD="word" FILES="file1.txt file2.txt" ./count_lines_with_word.sh
# 2) Or pass word and files as args: ./count_lines_with_word.sh word file1.txt file2.txt
# 3) Or pass word and read files from stdin: echo "..." | ./count_lines_with_word.sh word

word="${WORD:-$1}"
# if word came from arg, shift it off so $@ contains files
if [ -z "${WORD}" ]; then
  shift 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# If FILES env var is provided, use it (space-separated list)
if [ -n "${FILES}" ]; then
  set -- ${FILES}
fi

# If no files provided, read from stdin
if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
  # count distinct lines that contain the word (each matching line counted once)
  grep -w -- "${word}" | wc -l
else
  # count matching lines per file then sum
  grep -w -h -c -- "${word}" "$@" | awk '{s+=$1}END{print s+0}'
fi"}
